correctness.rationale: The dyadic recurrence yields s(2^r(2j+1)±1)=(r+1)a+rb and ra+(r+1)b with a=s(j),b=s(j+1); adjacent coprimality forces gcd(a-b,(2r+1)b)=gcd(a-b,2r+1). This proves the pointwise classification and complete divisor strata (construct j=2^(d+1)-1). For first appearances, r>=(d-1)/2 and j>=1, with equality achieved by j=1 where a=b=1. Reznick Theorem 4.7 equidistributes primitive Stern adjacent residue pairs modulo fixed m; direct primitive-pair count yields p-adic tail P(v_p(a-b)>=t)=p^(1-t)/(p+1), hence the stated local probability factors, CRT and the global absolutely summable r-mixture. Finite-independent recurrence arithmetic checked n<=49999 and first odd occurrences through 23, with exact primitive residue counts across six moduli. The external equidistribution theorem, not this finite enumeration, proves density.
residual_risks: An earlier name for next-nearest Stern gcd or a consequence buried in a broader valuation theorem may exist.
Density uses published fixed-modulus equidistribution; no uniform error rate in d is proved.
Independent enumeration is finite and not a substitute for asymptotic equidistribution.

originality.rationale: Reznick arXiv:math/0610601 Theorem 4.7 supplies equidistribution of consecutive Stern pairs, and his Section 2 provides dyadic identities; Allouche/Coons treat additive correlation. Neither inspected source states the two-step gcd law, complete divisor spectra, first appearances, record maxima and gcd-density distribution. Resultary and OEIS A002487 searches were checked for equivalent two-step claims; no exact covering source found.
